steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The right to a fair trial (Article 6 ECHR) includes the right to a hearing within a reasonable time, an independent tribunal, the presumption of innocence and the right to legal representation

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: In criminal cases, Article 6 guarantees the right to examine witnesses and to have the free assistance of an interpreter if needed

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The right to jury trial in England and Wales applies to indictable offences tried in the Crown Court, providing lay participation in the justice system

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Freedom of expression (Article 10 ECHR) protects the right to hold opinions and to receive and impart information and ideas without interference by public authority

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When writing about qualified rights, always apply the three-stage test: prescribed by law, legitimate aim, necessary in a democratic society Use specific examples to illustrate rights — e.g. the right to a fair trial includes specific guarantees such as the presumption of innocence When discussing legal aid, mention LASPO 2012 and the justice gap — this shows up-to-date knowledge Balance rights and responsibilities in your answers; the law restricts rights where they conflict with the rights of others or the public interest Remember that the Rule of Law underpins all citizen rights: no one is above the law and everyone has equal access to justice in theory
